reviews.outlet: design4real blog: World Labs Marble in practical testing
reviews.author: Clarence Dadson (CEO of design4real, a Munich VR/AR/3D-scanning agency)
reviews.summary: Hands-on in browser, VR headset and game engines. Worlds look striking at the centre but blur toward the edges, and the convincing walkable area is small. Paid splat exports carry the same blur, and the splat-derived meshes were poor. In Unity/Unreal, splats were GPU-heavy and mixing them with meshes caused depth and collision problems. Judged good for concept work and early experiments, not production or real-time.
reviews.note: No numeric score; the rating is our reading. The model version isn't stated (likely Marble 1.1, given the date). The agency sells VR/3D services and has no stated link to World Labs.

reviews.author: 梦瑶 (Mengyao)
reviews.summary: Same input image (a Minecraft-style render) through Marble 1.1 and 1.1-Plus. 1.1 produced a navigable world in about 3-5 minutes with a faithful reproduction, little noise and fuller lighting. 1.1-Plus gave a wider world but took twice as long and looked noticeably softer. The author recommends 1.1.
reviews.note: Short single-image test in Chinese, a news-style hands-on with no game-engine export tested. It compares only against Marble's own models.

reviews.outlet: Tech Insider: Genie 3 vs Marble vs NVIDIA Cosmos
reviews.author: Marcus Chen
reviews.summary: Calls Marble the most production-ready option thanks to exportable splats and a free tier, but says every comparison point is still demo-based or vendor-reported.

users.note: All 7 mentions come from one HN thread at launch (Nov 2025, Marble 1.0, before Marble 1.1 in Apr 2026). Comments only about future potential (lightcrafter, MarsIronPI) or the technique (kkukshtel) were left out as not about output quality. A second HN thread (45528320, a Labubu game using Marble worlds) had no quality opinions. No review-site rating pages found (Trustpilot and Product Hunt slugs returned 404).

vendor_claims.text: Marble 1.1 (Apr 2026) became the default, with claimed better lighting/contrast and fewer artifacts at the same 1,500 credits per world. 1.1 Plus expands world size for extra credits.
Exports full (2M) and 500k Gaussian splats (PLY/SPZ) plus collider and high-quality GLB meshes. Unity and Unreal splat plugin guides are in the docs.

strengths: Faithful to the input image, with good lighting (1.1)
Splat/mesh export with engine plugin paths
weaknesses: Small convincing area; blurs away from the centre
Splats are GPU-heavy and awkward to mix with meshes in engines
world-labs-marble.notes: No benchmark covers Marble: it isn't on WorldScore (checked leaderboard.csv in the HF space, updated 2026-09-10) or 3D Arena (object models only). Current models: Marble 1.1 (default) and 1.1 Plus, released Apr 2026. Sketchfab search for Marble-made models found none.

users.note: Below the 3-mention minimum, so not scorable. GitHub repo: 3.0k stars, 267 forks; an issues search for 'quality' returned only #22 (a request for higher-resolution panoramas).

vendor_claims.text: README (Jul 2025) claims it beats Diffusion360, MVDiffusion, PanFusion, LayerPano3D, Director3D, WonderJourney and DimensionX on BRISQUE, NIQE, Q-Align and CLIP for panorama and world generation. These are self-reported, with no protocol details.

hunyuanworld.notes: HunyuanWorld 1.0 (26 Jul 2025) has been superseded by Tencent's own HY-WorldPlay/HunyuanWorld-1.5 (Dec 2025) and HY-World-2.0 (16 Apr 2026, github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-World-2.0), per the 1.0 README. Tencent's HunyuanWorld-Voyager (a separate RGB-D video model) leads WorldScore's 3D group at 77.62 static, but under the runbook that is a different model and must not be scored for 1.0. HunyuanWorld 1.0 itself is not on WorldScore. Academic comparisons that include 1.0 as a baseline are by competing model makers (excluded by rule). A Sketchfab 'sci-fi room 1' (alexhuang0771, CC BY) says it was made with Tencent's hosted 'Hunyuan 3D interactive world generation', which is not the open 1.0 weights, so it was not used. Consider relisting as HY-World 2.0.

vendor_claims.text: Generates style-consistent concept art, then 3D props, true-scale wall/door/window kits and whole buildings from a floor plan. The showcase is a Georgian estate with 334 props, built 'in a single day', exported to Unreal.
Live on Google Cloud Marketplace for studios (28 Mar 2026). A self-serve plan for indie/solo users is behind a waitlist, with a preview announced 25 May 2026.

dreamlands.notes: No independent evidence: no benchmarks, reviews, ratings or community threads found. Its site names no customers, founders or press coverage. Timeline per its blog: GCP Marketplace Mar 2026, preview May 2026 (the 'Oct 2026 launch' in our brief may be the self-serve opening; not confirmed).

ratings.note: Launched about a year ago; no reviews.

vendor_claims.text: Places generated 3D models, materials, Niagara effects and sounds into the project with collision. It also claims PCG graph generation and rule-based scatter, plus a demo of 'dressing' a greybox hangar. Testimonials on the site don't mention level building.

ludus-ai.notes: No independent evidence on its level-building side. StraySpark has a Ludus-related post (ai-unreal-engine-data-policies-aura-ludus-epic-cloud-2026), but StraySpark sells competing Unreal MCP tooling and the post is about data policies, so it was not used.

general_sources.note: Last updated 2026-09-10. It has 35 entries (21 video, 9 3D, 5 4D). None of our four tools is on it. Most 2026 entries were 'Sampled by / Evaluated by' their own teams, which isn't blind or independent.

caveats: 1) We found no independent benchmark that includes Marble, HunyuanWorld 1.0, Dreamlands or Ludus AI. WorldScore covers only research/open models, and its newer rows are self-evaluated. All benchmark arrays are empty. 2) Only Marble has independent hands-on reviews (2 scored). HunyuanWorld 1.0 has none that we found, and its community sample is below the minimum. 3) Our WebSearch budget (shared across the session) ran out partway through this job. We could not search for YouTube hands-on tests, 80.lv/CG Channel/UploadVR coverage of Marble, HunyuanWorld hands-on posts, or Dreamlands launch coverage. Gaps partly reflect that, not only absence of evidence. 4) Marble's community sample is a single launch-week HN thread on Marble 1.0. 5) Reddit and X were skipped per instructions. 6) Ludus AI is a side tool here; its level features aren't covered by anything independent.
